title: A flyer on which branch?
hook: Some flying reptiles lived alongside dinosaurs.

doesNotKnow: Distinguish pterosaurs from Dinosauria using a simplified tree.

misconception: Every flying Mesozoic reptile was a dinosaur.
objective: Distinguish pterosaurs from Dinosauria using a simplified tree.

claims.text: Some flying reptiles lived alongside dinosaurs. On this simplified family tree, are pterosaurs inside the dinosaur branch? The pterosaur branch and the dinosaur branch share an earlier ancestor. The pterosaur branch lies outside the highlighted dinosaur branch. Flying does not by itself make an animal a dinosaur.
claims.source: Source leads to verify: Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History, https://naturalhistory.si.edu/collections/paleobiology; Natural History Museum, https://www.nhm.ac.uk/discover/dino-directory.html.

claims.text: Recall: A pterosaur and a dinosaur share an ancestor outside the dinosaur branch. Which is true? Sharing an earlier ancestor does not put the neighboring branch inside Dinosauria.
claims.source: Source leads to verify: Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History, https://naturalhistory.si.edu/collections/paleobiology; Natural History Museum, https://www.nhm.ac.uk/discover/dino-directory.html.

recall.question: A pterosaur and a dinosaur share an ancestor outside the dinosaur branch. Which is true?
options: The pterosaur is automatically a dinosaur
The groups have no shared ancestor
The pterosaur is outside that dinosaur branch
recall.why: Sharing an earlier ancestor does not put the neighboring branch inside Dinosauria.
